name: event-streaming-analytics
description: Event Hubs ingestion, a Stream Analytics job shaping events to a curated lake, a Functions hot-path consumer, and Cosmos DB serving - all keyless.
what: Devices and apps publish to an Event Hubs namespace. A Stream Analytics job reads one consumer group, applies a windowed transformation, and lands curated Parquet in an ADLS-style container. An isolated-worker Functions app reads a second consumer group for the low-latency hot path and writes to a serverless Cosmos DB serving store. Event Hubs, Stream Analytics, and Functions all authenticate with managed identity (local auth disabled).
why: Telemetry, clickstream, and IoT scenarios need both a cheap durable cold path and a low-latency hot path off the same ingestion stream. This separates concerns with managed services so there are no Kafka clusters or polling jobs to operate, and no SAS keys to rotate.
potentialUseCases: IoT / fleet telemetry ingestion and curation
Fraud / anomaly hot path with a durable replay log
Operational metrics fan-out to a serving store and a lake

reliability: Zone-redundant Event Hubs, storage, and Cosmos in prod
Two consumer groups isolate hot and cold consumers
security: Local auth disabled on Event Hubs; all consumers use managed identity
Identity-based Functions host storage (no connection strings)
Cosmos data-plane access via SQL RBAC
costOptimization: Standard Event Hubs auto-inflate and Y1 consumption Functions in dev
operationalExcellence: Application Insights + Log Analytics on the Functions app
Declarative Stream Analytics query and bindings in IaC
performanceEfficiency: Partitioned event hub scales consumer parallelism
Elastic Premium Functions scale out for the hot path

cost.profile: Prod profile: Premium Event Hubs, 6 SU Stream Analytics, EP1 Functions.
